newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down on poll result.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down on poll result.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen down on Monday on expectations of negative reaction to Sunday's poll results and profit-taking after recent gains, analysts said.
The New Aspiration Party won yesterday's Thai election by a wafer thin margin and was set to forge a coalition this week with member parties of the outgoing coalition government.
"Many people believe it is the same as the last government but with a change of leader," said Nakorn Kolfrichai, executive vice-president at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities.
"For the short term maybe there is some negative impact because many investors thought the Democrats might win."

"I think people will be waiting two or three more days to see what happens," Nakorn said, referring to talks under way between NAP leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and prospective coalition allies to set up a new government and cabinet.
Brokers said economic management of the new administration would be as key to longer term sentiment.
"I think people will wait and see if the economic team has enough of an independent charter to carry out what is necessary," said Ma Hui Hsing, director investment banking at General Finance.
